fact_check.claim: An appeal is a request to reconsider the specific information provided on the financial aid application; approved appeal lowers EFC and raises grant or endowed scholarship aid
fact_check.note: Page says an appeal reconsiders information on the CSS Profile/FAFSA; if approved the EFC decreases and need-based aid such as a grant or endowed scholarship may increase.

fact_check.claim: Cornell gives need-based aid only, offers no merit aid and does not negotiate; decisions case by case
fact_check.note: Page states need-based aid only and that it does not negotiate; case-by-case decisions confirmed by search snippet.

fact_check.claim: May be considered: application errors (misreported income, assets, family size)
fact_check.note: Listed as stated.

fact_check.claim: May be considered: major family changes (parental abandonment or estrangement, death or incarceration of a parent)
fact_check.note: Listed (plus human trafficking and refugee/asylee status, omitted by the article, which says 'for example').

fact_check.claim: May be considered: involuntary job loss with significant income reduction, excessive unreimbursed medical expenses, 'one-time income or expenses tied to an emergency', unreimbursed natural disaster expenses
fact_check.note: Page lists 'one-time emergency-related costs' as considerable. 'One-time income' appears on the TYPICALLY DENIED list, so the article's wording wrongly puts one-time income under what may be considered.

fact_check.claim: Cannot consider a request to match another school's merit aid; typically denied: voluntary job loss, anticipated or very recent job loss, recent divorce or separation
fact_check.note: All appear on the cannot-consider / typically-denied lists.

fact_check.claim: Medical, dental and vision expenses, including copays and premiums, are generally not considered; excessive unreimbursed medical expenses can be
fact_check.note: Page says these are generally excluded unless they fall under a special circumstance.

fact_check.claim: Undergraduate college costs for older siblings are generally not considered
fact_check.note: Listed among items already considered.

fact_check.claim: Private K-12 costs for younger siblings are not considered 'unless tied to a special or unusual circumstance'
fact_check.note: Page lists private K-12 costs for younger siblings as already considered; the fetched text did not show an 'unless tied to a special or unusual circumstance' qualifier for siblings (the 'unless special circumstance' wording applies to medical costs and to non-contributing parents).

fact_check.claim: Documentation, as opposed to persuasion, is key; incomplete or insufficient appeals may be denied
fact_check.note: Denial wording confirmed ('incomplete or insufficient documentation cannot be considered and may be denied'). The phrase 'documentation, as opposed to persuasion, is key' was not found in the fetched text, so the linked claim is unconfirmed.

fact_check.claim: Cornell's pages stress documentation but do not list documents for each circumstance
fact_check.note: Page says appeals 'require supporting documentation' and lists no specific documents.

fact_check.claim: Correct errors in CSS Profile/FAFSA and email finaid@cornell.edu; corrections may not require an appeal
fact_check.note: Confirmed; email finaid@cornell.edu confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Upload your documents first, through Cornell's secure upload page
fact_check.note: Page says submit requested documents first; 'secure upload page' not confirmed in the fetched text and is unlinked.

fact_check.claim: File the appeal after a preliminary estimate or official offer, using the Financial Aid Appeal Form with a short summary citing documents
fact_check.note: Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Appeals reviewed in order received; typical response 10 to 15 business days; no filing deadline listed
fact_check.note: Confirmed, including that no specific deadline is listed.

fact_check.claim: First-year and transfer students whose deposit depends on the result must request a deposit extension through the Admission Portal
fact_check.note: Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Phone 607-255-5145; counselor appointments by phone or video
fact_check.note: Phone +1 (607) 255-5145 and phone/virtual appointments confirmed.

fact_check.claim: EFC already $0 cannot be considered
fact_check.note: Listed under cannot be considered.

fact_check.claim: Approved appeals may not result in additional grant aid
fact_check.note: Page says approved appeals may not always result in additional grant or scholarship aid.

fact_check.claim: Cannot consider inability or refusal to pay the expected contribution or to borrow
fact_check.note: Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Cost of attendance increase request raises loan or work-study offer for allowable education costs above assigned budget
fact_check.note: Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: College Confidential: SchoolMatch said Cornell does not match offers; Momofthree24 said Cornell will review aid when a peer school offers more
fact_check.note: Both posts confirmed (Apr 3).

fact_check.claim: OP pxe wrote of an estimated cost of about $92K a year and a plan to appeal over price
fact_check.note: Confirmed; OP said they intend to appeal.

fact_check.claim: Replies from several posters, including blossom and Thorsmom66, said cost by itself is not grounds
fact_check.note: blossom said 'I don't feel comfortable paying' is not grounds, and tsbna44 said an appeal over not wanting to pay has essentially no chance. Thorsmom66 said receiving no aid suggests substantial investments, making aid unlikely on price alone; that is not the same statement.

fact_check.claim: Thread closed in September 2026 with no reported outcomes
fact_check.note: Auto-closed Sep 30, 2026; no one reports an appeal result.

fact_check.claim: CollegeXpress tells readers to share better offers in writing
fact_check.note: Page says 'share in writing the competing offer (or offers) you received' if the school is willing.

fact_check.claim: CollegeXpress says an appeal costs little because acceptance is not rescinded
fact_check.note: Page says you have nothing to lose and a college will not withdraw your acceptance for asking; the article's wording is a fair paraphrase, but the link text sounds like a quote.

beats_top.why: Cornell's own appeals page (same content as node/41699) is a list of rules with no situation-by-situation guidance, and it gives no sense of what to expect. Our page answers the question in the first paragraph, covers the exact situations students ask about and is candid that no success rates or first-hand wins exist. It will only beat the official page once the factual slips below are fixed.
changes: Correct the 'one-time income' error so the may-consider list matches Cornell's list.
Replace the unconfirmed 'documentation, as opposed to persuasion' phrase and the 'secure upload page' and sibling K-12 qualifiers with what the source says.
Link directly to the Financial Aid Appeal Form (https://www.finaid.cornell.edu/appeal-application) in the How to file steps so the page is complete as a one-stop guide.

fixes: In the bullet 'Substantial financial challenges beyond your family's control', change 'one-time income or expenses tied to an emergency' to 'one-time emergency-related costs'. Cornell lists one-time income among what is typically denied; source https://finaid.cornell.edu/node/41699.

In the Cost alone section, change 'Replies from several posters, including blossom and Thorsmom66, said cost by itself is not grounds' to credit blossom (said 'I don't feel comfortable paying' is not grounds) and tsbna44 (said an appeal over not wanting to pay has essentially no chance). Drop Thorsmom66, who only said aid is unlikely when no aid was offered.

In the paragraph under the table, remove the link text 'documentation, as opposed to persuasion, is key' (not found on the page). Replace it with the wording the page does carry: appeals 'submitted with incomplete or insufficient documentation cannot be considered and may be denied' (a short phrase, linked to https://finaid.cornell.edu/node/41699).

In the Sibling section, delete 'unless tied to a special or unusual circumstance' as applied to private K-12 costs for younger siblings, because the source lists these as already considered with no such qualifier. Keep the advice to appeal on a separate qualifying event as 'our suggestion'.

In How to file step 2, change 'Upload your documents first, through Cornell's secure upload page' to 'Submit the documents Cornell asks for first' and link it to https://finaid.cornell.edu/node/41699, or add a link to the upload page if you find it on finaid.cornell.edu.

In the FAQ 'Does asking hurt?', change the link text from 'costs little because acceptance is not rescinded' to a plain paraphrase (CollegeXpress says a college will not withdraw your acceptance for asking and that you have 'nothing to lose').
In the How to file steps, link 'Financial Aid Appeal Form' to https://www.finaid.cornell.edu/appeal-application.
